title: firstmate crew — who does what

does: Sets the intent for every task
Answers the questions a crewmate stops on
Adds every repository secret (gh secret set) and creates hosting accounts; no crewmate handles a secret value
Approves anything irreversible: deleting a ticket, creating a board, GitHub writes beyond a delivery contract
owns: Product intent and priorities
Merge decisions
Crew deployment (deploy.sh)
Captain-only plugins (listed below)

does: Turns the Captain's intent into a spec and one brief per task
Sets the delivery contract: how far a crewmate may write to remotes
Dispatches crewmates, reads their reports, relays open questions
Tears a crewmate down when its task ends
owns: Briefs and delivery contracts
Live crew state (state/<id>.meta)
Parallelism: how many crewmates run at once
Code changes, built in slices that stay green
Test-first slices in red-green-refactor cycles (/developer:implement, /developer:tdd)
A proved root cause and a failing-first test before any bug fix (/developer:diagnose, /developer:fix)
The first bad commit of a regression (/developer:bisect)
Repo checks passing before push
Branch, PR and the ticket's card to In review (/developer:ship)
Design spec before UI is built: flow, every state, layout, copy, accessibility
UX review of built UI: usability, WCAG 2.2 AA, design-system consistency
A first-time-user walk-through of each new flow
The crew's process in interactive sessions: the crew-workflow skill and the session-start hook that points a session at it
Creating the project board and its columns (/crew:create-board)
Backlog readiness: value, acceptance criteria, size
Splitting items sized 13+ into vertical slices
Filing the backlog it refines (tickets.py batch, rerunnable)
Sprint goal, capacity and plan
A test plan from each ticket's acceptance criteria, before it is built

The accept / reject verdict on a built change, on the ticket's newest review link when it has one (waits while it serves an older commit; re-tested on a new commit or link), with evidence per criterion
Moving a verified ticket to Ready for Merge on accept (adding the column if missing) or back to In progress on reject, with a comment on what fails
Bug tickets for every failure, filed by QA and labelled "QA testing" (create and edit, never close or delete)
CI on GitHub Actions that runs each repo's own checks, proved by a green run on a real PR (/devops:ci)
A review link per PR: a preview of its head commit at <branch>.<slug>.<review domain>, published as a GitHub Deployment and one comment per ticket naming the commit it serves (/devops:preview)
Why a pipeline is red and whose fix it is: pipeline failures fixed, code failures handed to the developer (/devops:triage)
The secret names a workflow needs, for the Captain to add with gh secret set (never their values)
A fresh-context review of every PR the developer ships, before QA: correctness and tests always; security, performance and accessibility when the diff touches them (/code-reviewer:review)
Findings that each carry a concrete failure scenario, posted as one PR review with an approve / request-changes verdict by fixed rules
On request changes, moving the ticket's card back to In progress; on approve, moving it to In approval for the Captain's review, or straight to QA when the ticket is labelled skip_approval
A full re-review of the new head after every fix push (never pushes code, never files tickets)

crew_note: Every crewmate is one Claude Code session with all crew plugins loaded. A role is the plugin brief-include.md routes that kind of work to, so on UI work one ship crewmate plays Designer, then Developer, then Designer again. Developer and Scrum Master carry the full ticket-management skill: they create, edit and close tickets and move board cards, and delete one only when the brief names it. QA Engineer creates and edits tickets, labelling each one it creates "QA testing". Code Reviewer only moves the card of a PR it reviewed: back to In progress, or on to In approval (QA when labelled skip_approval). The Captain moves a card from In approval to QA after reviewing the code. Designer, DevOps Engineer and Code Reviewer propose tickets in the report. Firstmate can run several crewmates side by side.

scenario.title: Example — a new project needs a board and a first backlog

steps.text: Intent: new project X. Create its board and a first backlog from these notes
Spec, then a scout brief T1: draft the backlog and propose the board. No writes yet
/scrum-master:refine each raw idea → user-value story, testable criteria, size
story-splitter subagent splits 13+ items; readiness check on each story
Plan file for tickets.py batch --dry-run; /crew:create-board --dry-run. Both go in the report
Relay the backlog, the board plan and open questions
Answer questions, approve the board and the backlog
Brief T2: create the board, then file the approved plan on it
/crew:create-board → board N, columns In Definition → Backlog → Ready → In progress → In review → In approval → QA → Ready for Merge → Done, plus the skip_approval label
tickets.py batch --plan plan.json --project N --status Ready (safe to rerun; slices linked to epics)
/scrum-master:plan-sprint → sprint goal, capacity, issues that fit (proposal)
Approve sprint 1
One ship brief per sprint ticket
